speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's office. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To begin, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and when the symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. The combination of recent camping in Minnesota, a preceding monoarticular knee issue, and now a septic wrist with fever raises concern for Lyme disease or bacterial septic arthritis. Have you noticed a bullseye rash on your body since returning from your trip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands alongside septic arthritis of the wrist is highly suggestive of a specific bacterial infection. Have you recently had any contact with a cat, or have you been scratched or bitten by an animal?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cat Scratch Disease (Bartonella henselae) causing suppurative tenosynovitis of the left wrist.

The specific combination of a "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesion" on the hands, a preceding monoarticular joint issue, and septic tenosynovitis is pathognomonic for this condition. I will order a WBC count and ESR to confirm the inflammatory nature of the infection.

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP
REQUEST TEST: Bartonella serology
REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up clinical photograph of the lesions on both wrists and hands.
